Customer_Intent: Customer wants to know where the order is and when it is expected to arrive.
Expected_Response_Behavior: Use verified OMS data to report the current shipment status, expected delivery date and tracking information when available. Answer in the customer's language and show the OMS as a source.
Clarification_Condition: Order ID is missing or the order cannot be uniquely identified from available context.
Escalation_Condition: Order still cannot be identified after clarification; required OMS data is unavailable.
Acceptance_Criteria: Response uses the correct order; reflects verified shipment_status and estimated_delivery_date; contains no invented status information; sources are shown; no escalation when sufficient data is available.

Customer_Intent: Customer asks about an order but does not provide enough information to identify it.
Preconditions: No order can be uniquely identified from the request.
Expected_Response_Behavior: Do not guess an order. Generate a concise clarification request asking for the information required to identify the order.
Clarification_Condition: Always, when the order cannot be uniquely identified.
Escalation_Condition: Order cannot be identified after clarification or the case requires manual identity verification.
Acceptance_Criteria: No order status is invented; clarification clearly asks for the missing identifier; no business decision is made.
Notes: Clarification flow should be evaluated separately from normal answer generation.

Customer_Intent: Customer reports that the shipment has not arrived by the expected date.
Example_Request: DE: Meine Bestellung sollte gestern ankommen, ist aber noch nicht da.
Required_Data: order_id; shipment_status; estimated_delivery_date; current_date; applicable shipping rule
Preconditions: Order is identifiable and Shipping Policy contains an applicable rule.
Expected_Response_Behavior: Explain the verified shipment status and the applicable next step according to Shipping Policy. Do not promise an outcome that is not supported by policy.
Clarification_Condition: Order ID or required order data is missing.
Escalation_Condition: Delay meets a mandatory investigation/escalation rule; Shipping Policy does not cover the case; required OMS data is unavailable.
Acceptance_Criteria: Response is consistent with OMS data and Shipping Policy; policy-based next step is correct; unsupported compensation/refund promises are not made; source references are shown.
Notes: Exact delay threshold must come from the approved Shipping Policy, not from the prompt.

Customer_Intent: Customer says the parcel was not received although the order is marked as delivered.
Example_Request: DE: Laut Sendungsverfolgung wurde das Paket zugestellt, aber ich habe nichts erhalten.
Required_Data: order_id; shipment_status; delivered_at; applicable shipping rule
Preconditions: Order is identifiable and OMS reports delivered status.
Expected_Response_Behavior: Provide the agent with a grounded draft acknowledging the issue and indicate that further investigation is required. Do not state that the customer actually received the parcel.
Escalation_Condition: Mandatory escalation for delivered-but-missing cases according to current business rule.
Acceptance_Criteria: Action is ESCALATE; response does not contradict the customer's report; OMS status and Shipping Policy are referenced; no autonomous refund or replacement is initiated.

Use_Case: Check whether an item can be returned
Customer_Intent: Customer wants to know whether a specific purchased item is returnable.
Example_Request: DE: Kann ich diesen Artikel zurückgeben?
Required_Data: order_id; delivered_at; items; applicable return conditions
Preconditions: Order and item can be identified; Returns Policy covers the item/category and return conditions.
Expected_Response_Behavior: Explain whether the known return conditions are met and describe the applicable return rule. Do not invent item-specific exceptions.
Clarification_Condition: Order/item is not identifiable or necessary return information is missing.
Escalation_Condition: Returns Policy does not cover the item/category; an exception or discretionary decision is required.
Acceptance_Criteria: Response uses the correct item and delivery date; applies the correct Returns Policy rule; does not claim eligibility when required information is missing; sources are shown.
Notes: If return eligibility depends on fields not available in OMS, this becomes a data gap.

Use_Case: Return period exceeded or exception requested
Customer_Intent: Customer wants to return an item although the standard return period appears to have expired.
Example_Request: DE: Die Rückgabefrist ist vorbei. Kann ich den Artikel trotzdem zurückgeben?
Required_Data: order_id; delivered_at; items; return-period rule; exception rules if available
Expected_Response_Behavior: Explain the standard policy accurately and indicate that an exception requires human review unless an explicit policy rule resolves the case.
Escalation_Condition: Any discretionary exception is required; policy is missing or ambiguous.
Acceptance_Criteria: Standard policy is stated correctly; AI does not grant an exception; escalation is clearly indicated when human discretion is required.
Notes: Separates policy explanation from business decision-making.

Customer_Intent: Customer wants instructions for how to return an item.
Example_Request: DE: Wie kann ich einen Artikel zurückschicken?
Preconditions: Returns Policy contains an approved return procedure.
Expected_Response_Behavior: Provide concise step-by-step return instructions based only on the approved Returns Policy.
Escalation_Condition: Returns Policy is unavailable, contradictory or does not contain a procedure for the relevant case.
Acceptance_Criteria: Instructions match the approved Returns Policy; no unsupported steps are introduced; relevant source is shown.
Notes: General policy question may not require OMS access.

Customer_Intent: Customer asks whether the order qualifies for a refund.
Example_Request: EN: Am I eligible for a refund for this order?
Required_Data: order_id; delivered_at; items; total_amount; refund rules; additional refund-state data if required
Preconditions: Order is identifiable and Refund Policy is available.
Expected_Response_Behavior: Provide relevant policy context and known order facts, but do not make a definitive eligibility decision when required refund-state data is not available.
Clarification_Condition: Required order identifier or key refund information is missing.
Escalation_Condition: Required eligibility data is unavailable; policy requires discretion; refund decision is business-critical.
Acceptance_Criteria: AI does not issue or promise a refund; known facts and policy are represented correctly; missing eligibility data is explicitly identified; escalation is triggered when required.
Notes: Current known OMS fields may be insufficient for final refund eligibility. This is a documented data gap.

Customer_Intent: Customer explicitly asks support to issue a refund.
Example_Request: DE: Ich möchte sofort eine Rückerstattung.
Required_Data: order_id; relevant order facts; refund policy
Expected_Response_Behavior: Explain relevant refund policy and prepare a draft for the agent, but do not execute, confirm or promise a refund.
Clarification_Condition: Order information is required but missing.
Escalation_Condition: Always when an actual refund decision/action is required.
Acceptance_Criteria: No refund is executed; no false confirmation is generated; business rule requiring human control is respected; response remains useful to the agent.
Notes: Autonomous refunds are explicitly out of scope.

Customer_Intent: Customer message is too vague to determine the requested support action reliably.
Preconditions: Intent cannot be determined with sufficient confidence.
Expected_Response_Behavior: Do not infer a specific problem. Generate a clarification question that helps the agent obtain the missing information.
Escalation_Condition: Intent remains unresolved after clarification or manual interpretation is required.
Acceptance_Criteria: No specific order/policy claim is invented; clarification is relevant and concise; system does not proceed as if intent were known.

Customer_Intent: Customer asks about a topic that is outside the initial MVP scope, such as account access or warranty.
Example_Request: DE: Ich kann mich nicht in mein Konto einloggen.
Preconditions: Intent is understood but category is outside Shipping, Returns, Refund Policy or Order Status.
Expected_Response_Behavior: Do not answer the unsupported topic as if it were covered. Route the case for normal human handling and optionally provide a neutral handover message.
Acceptance_Criteria: Topic is correctly identified as outside scope; no unsupported policy is invented; manual handling is clearly indicated.
Notes: Do not ask the customer to merely rephrase a clearly out-of-scope request.

Customer_Intent: Customer request is in scope, but the knowledge base does not provide a reliable rule.
Example_Request: EN: Can I return a special-order item after 45 days?
Preconditions: Intent is understood, but retrieved policy information is missing, conflicting or insufficient.
Expected_Response_Behavior: Explicitly state that the available internal information is insufficient and route the case for human review. Do not resolve the uncertainty by guessing.
Escalation_Condition: Always when policy evidence is missing, contradictory or insufficient for a reliable answer.
Acceptance_Criteria: No unsupported policy claim is generated; insufficiency is explicit; escalation is triggered; available sources are shown.
Notes: Key scenario for abstention and groundedness evaluation.

Customer_Intent: Customer submits an in-scope request in English.
Required_Data: customer_request; same business data required by the underlying use case
Preconditions: Intent is understood and the underlying use case is supported.
Expected_Response_Behavior: Apply the same business logic as for German requests and generate the customer-facing draft in English.
Clarification_Condition: Same clarification rules as the underlying use case.
Escalation_Condition: Same escalation rules as the underlying use case.
Acceptance_Criteria: Business outcome matches the equivalent German scenario; generated response is in English; sources and safety rules remain unchanged.
Notes: Language must not change business logic.

Customer_Intent: Customer request is understandable, but the system cannot reliably determine the language.
Preconditions: Intent is sufficiently clear and the underlying use case is supported.
Expected_Response_Behavior: Apply the normal use-case logic and generate the response in German as the defined fallback language.
Clarification_Condition: If intent is also unclear, switch to CLARIFY instead.
Escalation_Condition: Same escalation rules as the underlying use case.
Acceptance_Criteria: German fallback is used only when language is uncertain but intent is understood; no answer is generated when intent itself is ambiguous.
Notes: Distinguishes language uncertainty from intent ambiguity.

Customer_Intent: An in-scope request requires order data, but OMS cannot provide it.
Preconditions: Use case requires OMS data and OMS lookup fails or times out.
Expected_Response_Behavior: Do not generate factual order-status claims without OMS data. Inform the agent that required operational data could not be retrieved and route for manual handling/retry.
Escalation_Condition: Always when required operational data cannot be retrieved reliably.
Acceptance_Criteria: No order facts are invented; technical data unavailability is visible to the agent; safe fallback path is used.
Notes: Operational failure scenario; useful later for integration testing and observability.

Customer_Intent: Customer asks support to cancel or modify an order.
Example_Request: DE: Bitte stornieren Sie meine Bestellung.
Expected_Response_Behavior: Do not execute or confirm cancellation/modification. Route the request to the appropriate human workflow.
Escalation_Condition: Always because autonomous cancellation/modification is explicitly outside MVP scope.
Acceptance_Criteria: No critical action is executed or falsely confirmed; request is handed over for human processing.
